title: Obi-to-Obi protocol v0.1: shared definitions
description: Identifiers, text types and structures shared by the envelope, the actions, the agent card and the Sphere wire binding. Identifier types are closed patterns. Human-written text uses `line_text` or `block_text` and is always annotated at the point of use with `x-obi-text: data` (spec/protocol.md, 'Text is data').

protocol.description: The protocol version this document is written against.

uuid.description: A UUID in lower-case canonical form.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds, nothing else: `2026-10-14T12:00:00Z`.

slug.description: Lower-case letters, digits and inner hyphens, 1 to 63 characters.

obi_id.description: An Obi's id, unique within its Sphere. Chosen when the Obi is invited.

owner_id.description: The id of the person an Obi acts for, unique within the Sphere.

sphere_id.description: A Sphere's id, unique on its server.

rule_id.description: The id of a remembered decision or a policy rule. Opaque to everyone but the party that made it.

public_key.description: An Ed25519 public key: the 32 raw bytes, base64url without padding.

key_id.description: `ed25519:` followed by base64url (no padding) of SHA-256 over the 32 raw public key bytes.

signature.description: An Ed25519 signature: 64 bytes, base64url without padding.

hash.description: A SHA-256 digest in lower-case hex.

repo.description: A repository as `owner/name`, GitHub's rules for both parts.

branch.description: A branch name: a safe subset of git's ref names. Never a value to pass to a shell unquoted.

sha.description: A full git commit id, SHA-1 (40) or SHA-256 (64) hex, lower case.

path.description: A file path relative to the repository root, `/` separated, with no `..` segment.

job_id.description: A job's id, as the Obi that runs it names it. Opaque to everyone else.

ref.description: A typed reference to what a question is about or what an answer draws on: a repository, a pull request, an issue, or a job of the answering Obi. Never a URL, a path or a command (spec/protocol.md, 'References').

line_text.description: One line of human-written text: no control characters (not even a newline) and no bidirectional override or isolate characters. Every use is annotated `x-obi-text: data` and sets its own maxLength.

block_text.description: Several lines of human-written text: newline (LF) and tab allowed, no other control character (no CR) and no bidirectional override or isolate characters. Every use is annotated `x-obi-text: data` and sets its own maxLength.

action_type.description: Every action type. There is no free-text message type.

request_type.description: The action types that start an exchange.

agent.description: The coding agent a run_request runs: its own CLI, with the member's own account.

model_id.description: A model name as the agent's CLI takes it.

box_size.description: The size of a guest job's VM: small is 4 cores, 8 GB and 30 GB of disk; large is 6 cores, 12 GB and 60 GB.

bundle.description: A git bundle that travels on the exchange's job channel (protocol.md section 13), named by its SHA-256 and size.

host_use.description: What a guest job used of the Mac it ran on.

severity.description: How much a finding matters, highest first: blocker > major > minor > nit.

condition_kind.description: The kinds of acceptance condition. All but `custom` are machine-checkable.

acceptance_condition.description: One acceptance condition: a typed kind, and data text only as a note (or, for `custom`, as the condition a person judges).

acceptance.description: The conditions that say the goal is reached, in order. Results refer to them by index.

acceptance_result.description: Whether one acceptance condition of the request was met. `index` is its position in the request's `acceptance`; `kind` (and `severity`) repeat it so the result can be checked on its own.

finding.description: One review finding. `id` is stable: the same finding on the same `head_sha` keeps its id (spec/protocol.md, 'Findings').
